# Codex 0.166.0 protocol source fixtures

These 38 JSON files are unchanged upstream generated JSON schemas, retrieved
from `openai/codex`, tag `rust-v0.166.0`, commit
`6ff1e1ca3b30fc8b914720681fcf5fe62e95f856` on 2026-11-01.
`InitializeParams.json` and `InitializeResponse.json` come from
`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/json/v1/`; every other file comes from
`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/json/v2/` with the same filename.

Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/6ff1e1ca3b30fc8b914720681fcf5fe62e95f856/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/json
License and notice: see `../UPSTREAM_LICENSE` and `../UPSTREAM_NOTICE`.

Comparison with the same official schema paths at `rust-v0.163.0`: 23 files
are JSON-equal, 15 differ; none changes its root required-property list.
Differences in this subset concern optional context-entry names, new ThreadItem
variants/metadata/error variants, optional managed requirements/storage/OTel,
and hook events/environmentId. RPNH's existing safe user/agent text projection
and empty hook discovery validate against the new schemas; those upstream
variants do not become new RPNH execution capabilities.

This is a selected source-contract fixture set, not a complete protocol export
and not output generated by a locally installed 0.166 binary. Tests validate
actual RPNH discovery/history/start notifications and terminal-race wire
notifications under a mocked lifecycle against applicable schemas. The race
fixture supplies fake session/control reconciliation, not a real Registry race. Other included request/notification schemas support contract inspection;
fixture presence alone does not mean that request was exercised or implemented.
Native TUI rendering, Unix-socket connectivity, stock-client lifecycle and real
model execution were not qualified by these fixtures. The old Bedrock startup
response is absent from this tag's schema tree; the legacy RPNH response remains
for existing pinned clients, without claiming it is a 0.166 protocol feature.
